claim: Kandy's defensive system was primarily layered across the approaches to the capital — mountain passes, elevated observation posts, chokepoints and artillery positions — rather than concentrated in a continuous bastioned enceinte around the urban core.
bounded_by: The sources positively document defence at entrances, passes, heights and artillery positions. They do not prove that Kandy never possessed any walls, stockades or local fortifications, nor that every surviving absence in the present city is original.
notes: Field trigger: visitors report that modern Kandy lacks the monumental bastions expected of a repeatedly invaded capital. The supported interpretation is a defence-in-depth landscape, not an unfortified city.
